name: Nitrofurantoin
summary: Urinary-tract antiseptic that concentrates in urine; first-line for uncomplicated cystitis with little systemic exposure.
mechanism: Reduced by bacterial flavoproteins to reactive intermediates that damage DNA, ribosomal proteins, and other cellular targets — multiple mechanisms limit resistance.
pharmacodynamics: Bacteriostatic or bactericidal depending on concentration; effective only where urine concentrations are high.

pharmacokinetics.bioavailability: Well absorbed orally but negligible systemic levels — concentrates in urine

dosing.adult: 100 mg PO every 12 hours (monohydrate/macrocrystals, e.g. Macrobid) for uncomplicated cystitis

safety.pregnancy: Contraindicated at term (hemolytic anemia in newborn); generally avoided in first trimester; contraindicated with G6PD deficiency
safety.lactation: Avoid in nursing mothers of infants < 1 month or with G6PD deficiency
warnings: Pulmonary toxicity — acute reactions and chronic fibrosis with prolonged use

clinicalPearls: Concentrates in urine — effective for cystitis but useless for pyelonephritis (no tissue levels)
Chronic use carries pulmonary fibrosis risk — limit duration
good: Narrow-spectrum, low-resistance option for uncomplicated lower UTI.
bad: Not for pyelonephritis or upper-tract infection; contraindicated in renal impairment (CrCl < 30) and G6PD deficiency.

provenance.notes: Curated from standard infectious-disease/pharmacology references. Values omitted where not confidently known — nothing invented.
